title: Packing a Picnic Basket
description: Gather familiar food containers, table items, and simple lunch words for an outdoor meal.
cardDescription: Gather familiar food containers, table items, and simple lunch words for an outdoor meal.
focus: The clues describe what is packed and how it is carried. A container and one of its parts have different names.
solvingTip: Look for food, a carrying object, or an eating utensil.
words: Meal prepared to be eaten outdoors
Woven carrying container for an outdoor meal
Insulated box used to carry chilled picnic food
Cloth or paper provided with a packed meal
Flat dish used for an outdoor serving
Small drinking vessel packed for a picnic
Pronged eating utensil in a picnic set
Bowl-ended utensil packed with an outdoor lunch
Food made with filling between pieces of bread
Prepared mixture often carried as a cold side dish
Produce such as apples or peaches in a picnic basket
Outer covering keeping packed food together
Removable top closing a picnic container
Part used to lift a picnic basket

answerNotes.COOLER: Cooler names an insulated carrying box. It does not mean a lower temperature in this clue.
answerNotes.WRAP: Wrap is a covering here. It differs from the food itself inside the covering.
answerNotes.LID: A lid closes the container’s top. A handle is the part used to carry it.
answerNotes.SANDWICH: A sandwich combines bread with a filling. The clue describes the food form rather than one fixed ingredient.

title: At the Ice-Cream Counter
description: Browse familiar frozen-dessert forms, toppings, and serving objects.
cardDescription: Browse familiar frozen-dessert forms, toppings, and serving objects.
focus: The clues identify what is served and the objects used to serve it. Several short words have a special meaning at the counter.
solvingTip: Check whether a clue asks for a dessert form, a flavor, or an added topping.
words: Edible tapered holder for ice cream
Small container holding an ice-cream serving
Ice-cream dessert topped with sauce or other additions
Drink combining a beverage with ice cream
Thick blended drink often made with ice cream
Flavor traditionally made from cured orchid pods
Cacao powder used to add chocolate flavor
Addition placed on a frozen dessert
Small red fruit often placed on a sundae
Tiny decorative piece scattered over a dessert
Utensil used to eat a cup of ice cream
Cold storage compartment keeping ice cream frozen
Paper square offered with a dripping dessert

answerNotes.SUNDAE: Sundae names the dessert. It sounds like Sunday, but its spelling is different.
answerNotes.FLOAT: Float is a drink with ice cream here. It does not mean a parade platform or the act of staying on water.
answerNotes.SCOOP: Scoop names a rounded portion in this clue. The same word can name the tool used to form it.
answerNotes.CONE: A cone is the tapered edible holder. It names the shape and container rather than the ice cream itself.

title: A Chair Beside the Campsite
description: Explore a relaxed summer campsite through familiar shelters, supports, and outdoor belongings.
cardDescription: Explore a relaxed summer campsite through familiar shelters, supports, and outdoor belongings.
focus: The clues name objects seen at a temporary camp. They identify vocabulary rather than explaining how to set up equipment.
solvingTip: Look for a shelter part, a support, or a place around the campsite.
words: Temporary place where people stay outdoors
Portable fabric shelter used at a campsite
Short ground fastening used with a tent
Long support holding a tent’s fabric up
Strong woven fabric used for some outdoor equipment
Cord helping hold a tent steady
Enclosed portable light used around a camp
Handheld electric light with a directed beam
Portable seat placed near a tent
To bend a camp chair into a smaller shape
Large inland body of water beside some campsites
Land at the edge of a lake
Surface beneath a tent or outdoor chair

answerNotes.GUYLINE: A guyline is a supporting cord. The word names a part rather than a whole tent.
answerNotes.CANVAS: Canvas is a strong woven fabric. It can also name a painting surface in another setting.
answerNotes.PEG: A peg fastens or marks a position in the ground. It differs from the longer supporting pole.
answerNotes.FLASHLIGHT: Flashlight is the usual American name for this handheld light. Torch is a common British term.

title: A Backyard Cookout Table
description: Meet familiar cookout equipment, serving objects, and foods through plain definitions.
cardDescription: Meet familiar cookout equipment, serving objects, and foods through plain definitions.
focus: The clues describe a gathering around outdoor cooking. They do not give cooking times or a preparation sequence.
solvingTip: Look for equipment, a serving object, a food, or a guest’s role.
words: Cooking surface associated with a backyard cookout
Carbon-rich fuel used in some outdoor grills
Gripping tool used to lift cookout food
Broad flat utensil used to turn or lift a portion
Protective garment worn over a cook’s clothes
Large dish carrying food to a cookout table
Grain often served on the cob at a summer gathering
Small bread used to hold a burger or other filling
Liquid or semiliquid accompaniment added to food
Long narrow support holding pieces of food together
Flat object used to carry several servings
Flat-topped furniture around which guests gather
Person invited to a backyard meal
To offer prepared food to someone

answerNotes.SKEWER: A skewer holds separate food pieces along its length. The clue identifies the object rather than a cooking method.
answerNotes.SPATULA: A spatula has a broad flat working end. Tongs grip between two arms instead.
answerNotes.PLATTER: A platter is a larger serving dish. It differs from an individual plate at a guest’s place.
answerNotes.BUN: A bun is a small bread here. The word can also describe a coiled hairstyle in another context.

title: By the Summer Boathouse
description: Visit a lakeside boathouse through familiar small boats, their parts, and the objects beside a dock.
cardDescription: Visit a lakeside boathouse through familiar small boats, their parts, and the objects beside a dock.
focus: The clues distinguish vessels from equipment and places along the shore. Shape and use supply the answers.
solvingTip: Check whether the clue names a boat, a boat part, or something used beside the water.
words: Building used to store small watercraft
Narrow open boat commonly moved with a paddle
Small narrow boat commonly paddled with a double-ended paddle
Long rowing implement often supported at the boat’s side
Handheld blade used to move a canoe
Buoyant garment worn to help a person stay afloat
Structure where a small boat can be secured
Platform extending over water on posts
Strong cord used to secure a boat
Tied fastening in a boating rope
Fitting around which a boat line can be secured
Main outer body of a boat
Place where a small-boat passenger sits
Land bordering the lake beside a boathouse

answerNotes.CANOE: A canoe is commonly open on top and paddled. The clue uses its familiar form rather than one material.
answerNotes.KAYAK: A kayak is commonly used with a double-ended paddle. The clue distinguishes it from a canoe’s usual paddle arrangement.
answerNotes.CLEAT: A boat cleat is a securing fitting. It is not the stud on a sports shoe in this setting.
answerNotes.LIFEJACKET: Life jacket is usually written as two words. The grid joins the letters into one entry.
